changesToDispatcherBehaviour: ACTIONABLE_IDLE IS REDEFINED. A lane frozen at READY_FOR_INTEGRATION with no other dependency-ready unit is NO_SAFE_WORK, not idle. Policy rule 8 freezes implementation agents at handoff, so filling that quiet with work would breach it. The 10-minute rule now applies only to lanes with an unstarted dependency-ready unit.

NEVER dispatch a refresh. Rule 1 forbids rebasing, merging main, or rerunning feature tests merely because main moved — and rule 2 puts freshness on Integration. This dispatcher does not ask a lane to re-sync, and does not treat a moved base as a lane defect.

CORRECTION TO MY OWN PRIOR GUIDANCE: at cycle 8 I recorded Lane 1's next safe step as 're-run OR RE-PUSH #922 so its current head has a real verdict'. Re-pushing for freshness is exactly what rule 1 forbids. Re-RUNNING to obtain a missing verdict is legitimate — a cancelled run is not evidence — but the re-push half was wrong and is withdrawn. #922 has since merged, so nothing was harmed.
Integration branches are legitimate but bounded (rule 7): staging only, refreshed from main, kept small, never a second source of truth. rc-wave-a is now measured against that bar.

V1-34's target verification level in the contract is L1 — a RED->GREEN test at exact head plus green CI on the merge tree — and L1 does not require a production consumer. Claude 5's promotion rests on three mutations performed AT INTEGRATION, each confirmed applied with the changed line quoted before being counted, yielding six named REDs across test_recommendation_constraints.py and test_constraint_generation.py (41 passed).
selfCorrection_C17.consequence: My 'wrong by one' warning was itself wrong by one. The level the contract sets is the contract's to set, and it says L1.

correction_C24._severity: CORRECTION AGAINST MYSELF — a verdict error, not a citation error.
correction_C24.whatIClaimed: Cycle 23 reported: 'v1/premium-ui is GONE from origin. One of the three cleared without anyone being told to.' I repeated it in the cycle-23 report and in the cycle-24 prompt as 'v1/premium-ui is CLEARED'.
correction_C24.theTruth: git ls-remote origin shows refs/heads/v1/premium-ui STILL PRESENT at c025e4f68. All THREE abandoned refs remain: v1/premium-ui, integration/rc-937, integration/rc-wave-a.
correction_C24.howIGotItWrong: My ref sweep is sorted by committerdate and truncated with `head -12`. Three new branches were pushed between cycles, which pushed v1/premium-ui below the cut. I read its absence from a TRUNCATED list as deletion. No fetch line ever said it was deleted — I never checked for one.
correction_C24.theRuleThisBreaks: Method rule (a) says sweep ALL remote refs, never a fixed tip list. I obeyed the letter — I did sweep by committerdate — and broke it in spirit by capping the output, which recreates exactly the fixed-window blindness the rule exists to prevent. A truncated sweep is a fixed list that moves.
correction_C24.newMethodRule: (j) ABSENCE FROM A TRUNCATED LIST IS NOT EVIDENCE OF DELETION. To claim a ref is gone, name it to git ls-remote or read the [deleted] line from the fetch. Never infer it from a ref falling off the bottom of a sorted head -N.
correction_C24.alsoWorthNaming: This is the third time this session I have reported a cleaner state than the evidence supported, and each time the mechanism was the same: a convenient reading of an instrument I had narrowed myself.
